mailbox.title: 📬 An email address for every agent
mailbox.body: Make one mailbox just for your agents (a fresh Gmail is perfect). Each agent gets its own address on it, so hotels, shops and landlords write to your assistant, not to you. Mail sent to an agent's address lands in its chat.
mailbox.how:
How it works: the app password lets OpenDot sign in to this mailbox and read and send mail as a mail app would. Every agent's address is an alias of the same mailbox, e.g. you+pip@gmail.com. Mail to it arrives in this inbox, and what agents send goes out from this account, and only after you say OK.
Use your own personal mailbox? Then your front-desk agent also reads new mail sent to your normal address. That's why a separate mailbox just for your agents is the better choice.

phoneAccount.title: 📞 Phone numbers
phoneAccount.body: Hook up a Twilio account once, then give each agent its own number. Texts and voicemails to that number go straight to that agent.
phoneAccount.saved: 📞 Saved. Give each agent a number from its card.

budget.title: 🔕 How often they can nudge you
budget.body: Things your agents do on their own can buzz your phone at most {{limit}} times a day, and never between {{from}}:00 and {{to}}:00. The rest waits in the Inbox, with one quiet line in the evening. Replies to you and questions only you can answer always come through.

page.title: 🪪 Identity
page.intro: Give an agent their own email address, phone number and calendar. Nothing is active until you set it up below — and anything that acts as you (sending, calling, spending) still needs your OK.
page.empty: No agents yet — hatch one from Chats first.

err.auth: That app password didn't work. Make sure you pasted the app password (not your normal password) and the address is right.
err.app_password: The server wants an app password, not your normal password. The steps above show where to make one.
err.basic_auth_off: Microsoft has switched off password sign-in for this mailbox, and OpenDot can't do Microsoft's own sign-in yet. A Gmail or Fastmail mailbox will work.
err.imap_off: IMAP is turned off for this mailbox. Switch it on in your mail settings and test again.
err.unsafe_login: The server blocked the login as unsafe. Check IMAP is on in your mail settings and that you pasted the 授权码 (authorization code).
err.dns: Couldn't find that server. Check the host name for typos.
err.unreachable: Couldn't reach the server. Check the host and port, and that this computer is online.
err.timeout: The server took too long to answer. Check the port, or try again in a minute.
err.tls: The secure connection didn't work. Usually the port and security setting don't match: 993 and 465 use SSL/TLS, 587 uses STARTTLS.
err.send_refused: Signed in fine, but the server wouldn't send the test email.

gmail.name: Gmail
steps: Turn on 2-Step Verification for this Google account. App passwords only show up once it's on.
Open App passwords, type a name like “OpenDot” and hit Create.
Copy the 16-letter password and paste it below. Spaces don't matter.
IMAP is already on for Gmail, so there's nothing else to do.
gmail.authHint: With Gmail, a new app password fixes this nine times out of ten.

outlook.name: Outlook / Hotmail
steps: Turn on two-step verification in your Microsoft account's security settings.
Create an app password (Security → Advanced security options → App passwords).
Paste it below.
outlook.warn: To be straight with you: Microsoft has been moving Outlook.com and Hotmail over to its own sign-in for mail apps, which OpenDot doesn't support yet. If Test says the password didn't work, a Gmail or Fastmail mailbox is the easy way round.
outlook.authHint: Microsoft may simply not accept app passwords on this account any more.

icloud.name: iCloud
steps: Make sure iCloud Mail is on and you have an @icloud.com address.
Sign in at account.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords, and make one called “OpenDot”.
Paste it below, with your full @icloud.com address.

fastmail.name: Fastmail
steps: In Fastmail, go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Manage app passwords and access.
Click New app password, give it access to mail (IMAP/SMTP) and generate it.
Paste it below.

qq.name: QQ Mail
steps: On the QQ Mail website: Settings → Account (账号与安全), and switch on the IMAP/SMTP service.
Confirm with your phone and you'll get a 16-letter authorization code (授权码).
Paste that code below. It's not your QQ password.
qq.authHint: QQ Mail only accepts the authorization code (授权码), never your QQ password.

netease.name: 163 Mail
steps: On the 163 Mail website: Settings → POP3/SMTP/IMAP, and switch on the IMAP/SMTP service.
Confirm as asked and you'll get an authorization code (授权码). It's only shown once, so copy it.
Paste that code below. It's not your login password.
netease.authHint: 163 Mail only accepts the authorization code (授权码), never your login password.

other.name: Something else
steps: Look up your provider's IMAP and SMTP settings and fill them in under Server settings.
If they offer app passwords, use one instead of your normal password.
Sign up at Twilio (it's pay-as-you-go; numbers cost a dollar or so a month, texts a cent or two).
On the Twilio Console home page, find Account SID and Auth Token under Account Info.
Paste both below and hit Test & save.
twilio.trialNote: This is a trial account: it can only text and call numbers you've verified in Twilio, and messages start with a trial note. Upgrade in the Twilio Console when you're ready.
twilio.noNumbers: No numbers on this account yet. Get one below.

public.no_public_url: Twilio needs a public https link to reach OpenDot. Run ./dot.sh link (the Cloudflare link works), or set DOT_PUBLIC_URL, then press Fix it.
public.private_link: You're on a private Tailscale link, which Twilio can't reach. Set DOT_PUBLIC_URL to a public https address (for example a Cloudflare link or Tailscale Funnel), then press Fix it.
